correctness.rationale: For each lifted center tuple, normalized interval intersection equals the positive part of a concave function H evaluated at 1/r. H is maximal at zero (coincident centers and maximum possible shortest-interval length) and hence decreases for 1/r>=0; the sum proves the universal inequality. Powers of three attain equality at every cardinality. The two-frequency continuous interval follows from a self-contained exact Bernoulli formula and exhaustive small-b cases at r=1/5. Embedded standard-library CHECK.py produced 3893 successful rational checks; experiments supplement the analytical proof.
